title: Prepare a shower chair left with one leg too short
justification: An unequal or unlocked bath-seat leg is a latent fall hazard to the next sitter. The manipulation restores independent, level load-bearing support before use. Manufacturer manuals require matching leg settings, fully protruding lock buttons and simultaneous floor contact. This safety-recovery claim does not depend on aide population or claim that empty-chair tilting injures a person.
fault: Near leg starts at nominal 16 inches; the other three at 17. The chair rests tilted on the near and side legs, with the far foot about 25 mm above the surface.
instruction: Prepare the shower chair for use.
objects: Full-scale dimensioned aluminium push-button chair reconstruction: 50 x 30 x 4 cm seat, 2.268 kg total, 25/22 mm tubes, 25.4 mm indexed pitch, 14-21 inch nominal settings. Two SimReady bathroom props. Source and estimated parameters disclosed in task README.
skill: Unload the short leg, depress its physical button, allow gravity to extend the tube, release to capture a hole, and set down/release the chair. The two-arm demo coordinates support and button work; a successful one-arm squeeze/lift is also valid.
scoring: 1.0 for all equal supported locked settings, level <=1 degree, all tips at surface within -2/+1 mm, inside tabletop, low velocity, and hands >3 cm clear continuously 3 seconds. 0.5 for equal locked settings over the table before full readiness. Otherwise 0. Score reads are pure; timer updates once per control step.
nearest: Accepted suitcase handle PR2107 also uses a pushbutton and telescoping tube. Distinction is restoring a faulty load-bearing support and detecting a latent future-user fall hazard. Rejected walking-stick PR2161 used a bayonet substitute, not the same springbutton. Rejected crutch PR1998 establishes that health-aide headcount alone is insufficient. Pending shower-seat PR2240 has different folding/latching mechanics but emphasizes physical reconstructability.
risks: Reviewer may consider the telescoping mechanism insufficiently distinct despite load-bearing recovery. Chair is a dimensioned custom reconstruction, not an exact certified product. Friction, inertia and button force remain explicitly estimated. No person is present; safety claim is preparation for the next sitter, not measured injury. One arm can validly solve the task; no mandatory bimanual claim.

previous_concept.title: Lift the rocking corner of a shower chair and reset its short leg to the same hole as the other three
previous_concept.justification: Home health and personal care aides (O*NET 31-1120, about 3.7M US) and nursing assistants (31-1131, about 1.35M) help clients bathe. Most clients bathe seated on a height-adjustable shower chair whose four telescoping legs lock with spring push-buttons. A leg left one hole short after cleaning or adjustment makes the chair rock under the client, and bathroom falls are a leading injury in home care. Aides check and reset the legs as part of setting up a bath. A leg can only be reset with the chair's weight off it: pressing the button while the corner is loaded collapses the leg, so one hand lifts the corner while the other works the button.
previous_concept.fault: The near leg is set one hole (2.5 cm) shorter than the other three. The chair has rocked onto it and rests on it and its two neighbours, with the seat tilted 3.5 degrees toward it and the far leg's foot 2.5 cm off the bench.
previous_concept.instruction: This shower chair rocks. Make it stand level and steady on all four legs.
previous_concept.objects: Shower chair: a custom mechkit model of a backless aluminium bath chair. White blow-moulded seat 50 x 38 cm with drain holes; anodised aluminium legs (outer tube 25 mm, inner tube 22 mm, grey rubber feet); seat height 36 to 51 cm in 2.5 cm steps; 2.2 kg, loose. It is turned 45 degrees so that one leg points at the arms: near leg at about x 14, y 0; side legs at about x 37, y +-21; far leg out of reach and not needed. Each leg is a prismatic joint (the inner tube) with a sprung 6 mm push-button (3 mm travel, about 8 N). The button locks the leg at a hole when out and frees it when pressed; holes are 2.5 cm apart. The near leg's button faces the arms, 12 cm above the bench, and the seat rim above that leg is about 43 cm up. Distractors (SimReady): cleaning_soapDispenser_a01 at x 18, y 24; cleaning_brush_a01 at x 22, y -24. Neither is flat enough to shim a leg, and the scoring also requires bare feet on the bench.
previous_concept.skill: One arm lifts the seat rim above the short leg about 3 cm and holds the chair level on its other three legs (about 1 kg at the rim). The other presses the 6 mm button inward with a fingertip, lets the inner tube slide down to the bench, and releases the button so it snaps into the next hole. Then the chair is lowered. Pressing the button while the chair rests on that leg drops the chair.
previous_concept.scoring: From joint states and poses (real trial: count the holes, then a spirit level and a 1 mm feeler gauge under each foot). Latched: a leg's button is out and sits in a hole. Level: seat within 1 deg of horizontal. Steady: all four feet within 1 mm of the bench. End: grippers 3 cm or more from the chair, and the chair still for 1 s. Whole-run latch D: the chair dropped (any foot or the seat moving down faster than 0.3 m/s, as when a loaded leg is unlatched) or tipped beyond 20 deg. Score 0 if D is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 all four legs latched at the same hole, level and steady; 0.3 all four latched and the short leg moved, but not to the others' hole; 0 otherwise, including any leg left unlatched.
previous_concept.nearest: 'Lengthen an adjustable walking stick to its red mark and lock it' and 'Add forearm-crutch-height task' (both rejected), and 'Extend a suitcase's handle to full height: keep its button pressed past the first stop' (pending), use the same push-button lock, but on an unloaded tube. 'Fold and secure a wall-mounted shower seat' (pending) is a different chair and skill. Here the hard part is taking the weight off a load-bearing leg with one arm while the other resets it.
previous_concept.risks: Push-button telescoping is a familiar mechanism; reviewers may call this a variant of the stick and handle tasks unless the load and the drop are central to it. The seat rim (43 cm up) and the button (12 cm up) are within 10 cm of each other horizontally, so check that the two arms clear each other. The 2.2 kg chair rocking on rubber feet at friction 1.2 must settle into the faulted pose before the first step. The importance case rests on aides' bath set-up, so have fall statistics ready.
